title: Exploit Chain: Unauthenticated error-oracle (CWE-209) + unauthenticated PII writes (CWE-287) - recon to DB abuse
description: Step 1 (Finding: unauthenticated writes): attacker sends arbitrary JSON to POST /api/leads/create with no auth, rate limit or CSRF (lead.py:10). Step 2 (Finding: raw exception text): by triggering server-side exceptions on that same endpoint (verified: an unauthenticated request returned HTTP 400 with the full SQLAlchemy error including the INSERT statement, bound parameters, and internal module paths), the attacker harvests internal intel: SQL dialect details, parameter values, code layout, DB state. Step 3: with the error oracle confirmed and no throttling, the attacker floods the endpoint with valid payloads (verified HTTP 200 + row persistence) to pollute the leads PII table, consume disk, and spam sales follow-up. The /docs exposure (DEBUG default True) fuels Step 2 by publishing the exact request schema.
impact: Compounded impact: internal information disclosure (SQL, parameters, paths) + unbounded PII database pollution and disk growth, all unauthenticated - higher than either finding alone (recon data feeds the abuse, and the abuse feeds more recon through the error oracle).
mitigation: Fix at least one link: add authentication/rate limiting to the lead endpoint, replace detail=str(e) with a generic error mapping (log details server-side), and default DEBUG=False to hide /docs.
